transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Mark Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Omar Reyes (Redwood SE), Sarah Chen (Nimbus CTO), Alex Rivera (Nimbus ML Eng), Liam O'Connor (Nimbus Security), Maya Patel (Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
- Quick overview of Redwood API and runtime
- Parity mapping discussion for existing prompts and endpoints across OpenAI/Anthropic/Together
- Security controls and private deployment options discussed
- Agreed to pilot (2-week perf POC) and share pricing/security docs

[00:00] Mark Liu (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Mark, i'm the AE on the account, and with me is priya and omar from our se team. how's it going over on your side?
[00:10] Sarah Chen (Nimbus): hey, thanks for doing this. good, excited to see the mapping. we've been running mixed traffic across openai and anthropic and some together models for a few features.
[00:20] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): yep i mainly do the embeddings and our chat pipelines, curious how much work it'll be to switch and where we lose any features.
[00:30] Priya Patel (Redwood): great, totally. today's plan: quick product walkthrough of the api and console, then focus on parity mapping — endpoints, params, streaming, function calling — and then security and next steps. sound good?
[00:37] Maya Patel (Nimbus): sounds good.
[00:40] Mark Liu (Redwood): quick qualifying q: what are your main success criteria for this migration? latency, cost, data isolation?
[00:47] Liam O'Connor (Nimbus): security first, we need SOC2 and KMS support. also latency for real-time chat must stay under 300ms p50 ideally. cost is a factor but not the blocker.
[01:00] Sarah Chen (Nimbus): timeline is quarter end preferably, but we'll do a pilot first.

[01:15] Priya Patel (Redwood): ok good. so mapping summary: the Redwood API uses a similar REST surface — you can do generation, chat, embeddings, rerank. for model names we expose curated open models, and we also offer streaming plus function/tool calling. function calling is a one-to-one mapping to openai style but with small naming differences in the proto. we'll share the sample client snippets.
[01:38] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): cool, can you map anthroipic's chat schema to yours? sometimes anthropic has slightly different system message semantics.
[01:49] Priya Patel (Redwood): yep. for claification, anthropic's system->assistant role swaps are typically handled at the prompt layer, we provide a compatibility shim in the SDK that accepts openai or anthropic style payloads and normalizes it to our runtime. occasionally you see small output differences because decoding defaults differ, but we can set sampling, temp, top_p, and logit bias equivalently.

[02:10] Omar Reyes (Redwood): also on tokenization parity — we support the common bpe tokenizers; when you run the parity mapping spreadsheet we'll calculate relative token counts so you can see cost delta.
[02:22] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): nice. what about streaming? we have a streaming UI and rely on partial tokens.
[02:29] Priya Patel (Redwood): streaming is supported, you can get chunked events similar to openai's chunked delta payloads. small note: our event envelope uses "chunk_id" and sometimes the order contains flush events; i.e. in one of our earlier transcripts the client mis-parsed chunk vs final. just something to be aware of.

[03:00] Sarah Chen (Nimbus): on the topic of function calling, we have heavy usage for structured actions. is your function calling deterministic? we need the same behavior across models.
[03:10] Priya Patel (Redwood): function calling is deterministic when using the same decoding params and model variant; we also surface a "function_call" flag you can set to 'force' or 'auto' like openai. small name mismatch of the fields sometimes in the SDK but it's documented. we'll include sample cURL and js snippets.

[03:45] Liam O'Connor (Nimbus): security — what's the process for private deployments? we might need a vpc and kms in our aws account. do you support customer-managed kms?
[03:55] Mark Liu (Redwood): yes, our Private offering supports customer KMS/HSM and VPC peering. for enterprise we also provide audit logs, RBAC via SAML/SSO, and retention controls. we can do on-prem for air-gapped if needed. we'll share the security pack.

[04:20] Maya Patel (Nimbus): any compliance certs?
[04:23] Mark Liu (Redwood): SOC 2 Type II and in process for ISO; i'll send the artifacts. (note: previously we had an older SOC two doc; apologies if the name got mangled in the notes).

[04:40] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): performance — your benchmarks vs openai for p50 latency?
[04:45] Omar Reyes (Redwood): depends on model and token length; for short-chat tokens we regularly hit ~80-180ms p50 on Dedicated for Curie-like open models; for larger models expect higher. important levers: batching, kv cache reuse, quantization. for hosted our multi-tenant latency will be slightly higher, dedicated gives predictable throughput.

[05:12] Sarah Chen (Nimbus): can you run a benchmark with our sample traffic and show token costs?
[05:16] Mark Liu (Redwood): absolutely — that's the POC we propose. we'll run bench with same prompts, same temperature, and provide token counts plus per-token cost estimates.

[05:30] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): about the model variants — how do you handle fallbacks? if our primary model is busy do you spill to another variant?
[05:39] Priya Patel (Redwood): we have smart routing policies: cost-first, latency-first, region preference; you can pin model versions and set fallback lists. e.g. pin to an Llama-2-variant and fallback to a quantized variant if capacity hits threshold. this preserves functionality but can change output subtly, so we recommend canary rollouts and eval sets.

[06:05] Sarah Chen (Nimbus): evals — we have a set of golden prompts to validate regression. can you tie alerts to regressions?
[06:12] Omar Reyes (Redwood): yes — Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring and regression alerts against prompt sets. we'll onboard your evals and set up a baseline and alert thresholds.

[06:30] Mark Liu (Redwood): quick demo — switching over to the console. (brief pause, screen share noises)
[06:40] Priya Patel (Redwood): here's the API explorer, you can paste an openai-style request and the SDK will translate. note the model catalog on the left, we tag by throughput/latency profile. also see the cost estimator on the right.
[07:00] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): i see reranking endpoints too, we use that for search re-rank. any compatibility issues?
[07:05] Priya Patel (Redwood): reranking maps to a separate endpoint; same semantics, just different payload shape, we'll include conversion examples.

[07:30] Mark Liu (Redwood): now the parity mapping spreadsheet — high level: we want to map every current endpoint, parameters, decoding settings, and sample prompts. we'll compute token diffs and suggested quantization/profiles.
[07:45] Maya Patel (Nimbus): that spreadsheet will be super helpful — can you include suggested batching settings?
[07:50] Priya Patel (Redwood): yes — we'll include batching and cache TTL recommendations per route. for chat UI low latency we recommend small batch sizes and cache prefix reuse. for embeddings batch more aggressively.

[08:10] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): last time we tested a quantized variant we saw some hallucination increase. how do you recommend balancing that?
[08:18] Omar Reyes (Redwood): tradeoffs depend on model family; we recommend AB tests on quality metrics. Optimize will flag regressions. quantization profiles we suggest start with 8-bit and then a light calibration run; we'll provide recommended profiles in the mapping doc.

[08:40] (brief cross talk)
[08:45] Sarah Chen (Nimbus): from infra side, who do we work with to set up VPCs and peering?
[08:50] Mark Liu (Redwood): Omar will be your infra SE contact for POC; he can share the runbook and network requirements.
[09:00] Omar Reyes (Redwood): i'll need a sample IP allowlist and an S3 bucket for logs if you want audit export. we'll provide terraform snippets for peering too.

[09:20] Liam O'Connor (Nimbus): about data residency — can you pin requests to region? we have eu data residency needs.
[09:27] Priya Patel (Redwood): yes region routing is supported and you can set tenant-level residency. private deployments give you full control if you need on-prem.

[09:40] Mark Liu (Redwood): let's walk through an example parity mapping for a chat prompt. (demo of pasted prompt) so you can see field-by-field how openai -> redwood mapping looks.
[09:55] Priya Patel (Redwood): example: openai param 'max_tokens' maps to 'max_output_tokens' in one of our older SDKs, but in the latest it's unified; occasionally our docs show the older name so ignore that. i note that openai's 'stop' behavior and anthropic's 'safety' constraints need explicit mapping; we add stop sequences at prompt compile time.
[10:25] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): we rely on logit bias heavily for safety gating — any differences?
[10:30] Priya Patel (Redwood): we support logit bias, but the per-token id mapping can change between tokenizers; our spreadsheet will include token ids to confirm. also we support per-route moderation hooks.

[11:00] Sarah Chen (Nimbus): any gotchas when switching embeddings providers? we use openai embeddings now for semantic search.
[11:08] Omar Reyes (Redwood): embeddings are straightforward; we provide cosine-ready vectors and provide similarity models. the main thing is vector dimensionality and normalization — we'll produce a conversion guide and show cost differences.

[11:35] Maya Patel (Nimbus): pricing — can you give rough numbers now?
[11:39] Mark Liu (Redwood): ballpark we'll send in doc; hosted is usage-based per token/embedding; dedicated is reserved commit with lower unit costs. i'll share a sample calc based on your current monthly token usage.

[12:00] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): for the POC, we want both functional parity and perf metrics. what's realistic?
[12:06] Priya Patel (Redwood): 2 weeks is reasonable: week 1 ingest parity prompts, run functional comparisons and adjust decoding params; week 2 ramp perf and benchmarking. we'll provide scripts and look at p50/p95 latency, token cost, and regression metrics.

[12:35] Liam O'Connor (Nimbus): security again: do you support SAML + SCIM provisioning?
[12:41] Mark Liu (Redwood): yes SAML SSO plus SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC can be customized. we'll include our SAML metadata and example SCIM endpoints.

[13:05] (small pause)
[13:10] Priya Patel (Redwood): quick demo snippet to show function-calling example mapped from openai style to our SDK. (snippets)
[13:25] Alex Rivera (Nimbus): looks similar enough. any SDKs we can use now?
[13:28] Mark Liu (Redwood): we have js/python/go SDKs and we also support direct REST for quick curl tests.

[13:45] Sarah Chen (Nimbus): ok timeline — once we get pricing and parity sheet we'll decide internal stakeholders and then kickoff POC?
[13:52] Mark Liu (Redwood): yep that's the plan. we'll also need a technical kickoff to exchange keys and configure a restricted dataset for benchmarks.

[14:05] Maya Patel (Nimbus): can you share the parity mapping template by tomorrow?
[14:08] Priya Patel (Redwood): we'll aim for tomorrow EOD.

[14:15] (wrap up)
[14:16] Mark Liu (Redwood): recap of next steps: Mark will send pricing and security docs, Priya will send parity mapping template, Omar will prepare benchmark runbook. Nimbus team to share SOC2 and sample prompt set. schedule the POC kickoff for next week.
[14:30] Sarah Chen (Nimbus): thanks all. excited to see the results.
[14:34] Mark Liu (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs. bye.

End transcript.
